payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery chemistry designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and extend storage-system life. Independent auditing corrected the earlier claim of 12,000 cycles: the governing cycle-life figure is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold. The battery’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, and projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop. The design separates power capacity, determined by stack size, from energy capacity, determined by tank size.
